selected.title: 0.00000000042 MOD 10 = 0.42000000000

expected_result_sets.query: select d, d mod 1 from t
expected_result_sets.rule: d values are exactly the multiset 10^-1 through 10^-27 (DECIMAL(65,30)); every MOD(d,1) must equal d numerically

expected_result_sets.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS mismatches FROM t WHERE NOT (d <=> MOD(d,1))

selected.reported_phenomenon: With correct loaded DECIMAL values, at least one leading-zero value yields the erroneous scale-amplified remainder described in cmain (historical examples m=d*10^9), and mismatches > 0. Record individual d,m pairs; a different unexpected pattern is other_anomaly pending attribution.
requirements: Fresh dedicated schema; InnoDB available
auto_increment_increment=1 and auto_increment_offset=1 so fresh SERIAL ids are 1..27
Verify 27 expected nonzero DECIMAL values before using MOD result as oracle
Record SQL mode and UPDATE conversion warnings
selected.resources: One table, 27 rows, no loops outside bounded source SQL; no privileged/global/file operations
selected.cleanup: DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t; only in this case-owned fresh schema
selected.failure_handling: CREATE/INSERT/UPDATE failure, incorrect data cardinality or exponent conversion prevents the MOD oracle; do not count it as the target phenomenon. Historical 5.7.5 fix note is context, not proof about 8.0 targets.
